faqs.q: How much will a wildlife job run in Staten Island?
faqs.a: The price turns on the species, the number of entry points, and whether young or cleanup are involved. A single squirrel entry sealed early is a much smaller job than a raccoon family or a bat colony. We inspect, explain the full scope, and quote it in writing before work starts.

faqs.q: Why are there so many squirrels in Staten Island attics?
faqs.a: Our crew's Staten Island work centers on raccoons and squirrels in single-family attics, Norway rats on the older North Shore, and opossums under decks along the Greenbelt. The pattern follows the housing and the habitat: staten island greenbelt keeps animals close, and once one finds a way into a roofline, chimney, or crawlspace here, it usually comes back until every entry is sealed. That is why we pair removal with proofing on every Staten Island job rather than just taking the animal out.

Staten Island.housing_era: Staten Island is the city's most suburban borough: postwar single-family homes and townhouses across the South Shore and mid-island, older Victorians and apartments on the North Shore, and wooded Greenbelt streets where big lots back onto forest. Decks, sheds, and mature canopy drive the raccoon and squirrel work.

Staten Island.wildlife_intro:
Staten Island keeps our crew busy with raccoons and squirrels in single-family attics, Norway rats on the older North Shore, and opossums under decks along the Greenbelt. Staten Island Greenbelt  gives wildlife food, water, and cover within a short run of almost every roof in town, and the housing does the rest — once an animal finds a soft soffit, an uncapped chimney, or a gap at the roofline, it treats the house as part of its territory.

The year has a rhythm in Staten Island. Fall pushes squirrels, raccoons, and rodents indoors ahead of winter; spring brings denning mothers looking for chimneys and attic corners; summer is when bat colonies are most visible in older homes and when young animals start ranging on their own. Most Staten Island jobs start with a full roofline and foundation inspection, then removal and sealing every entry we find, because closing only the obvious hole rarely holds.
